summary: Lassen National Forest steel lookout in Shasta County, built 1934; its cab was destroyed in a 1987 backfire and never rebuilt, but the steel tower remains.

facts.design: California Region 5 Plan BC-301 cabin on a 30-foot K-brace open steel tower
facts.status_note: The steel tower remains; the cab was destroyed in 1987 and not rebuilt.
facts.agency: US Forest Service, Lassen National Forest

events.note: Register: constructed for the Lassen National Forest in 1934
Relief guard Woodrow McCowan, with a permanent lookout due to take over on 10 June; Stanley Billings named as rim lookout in September. The item does not name this tower.
Cabin destroyed in a Forest Service backfire that escaped in high winds; not rebuilt

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The record lists the FFLOS value as gone. The register's Removed 1987 entry refers to the cabin; its text says the steel tower remains. The FFLA list marks the tower Standing*, which its key defines as a structure remaining with the cab no longer in place, consistent with the 1987 loss of the cabin.

notes_for_editor: Height 9.1 m is converted from the register's 30-foot tower figure; the register does not say whether that is tower height or cab-floor height. The 1938 Searchlight items name a rim lookout but not this one, so the link is likely, not confirmed. One web search did not confirm the 1934 or 1987 dates beyond the register and newspaper quotes. The FFLA key defines Standing* as a structure remaining with the cab no longer in place, which fits the 1987 loss. The 1987 Lassen County Times item names the Hat Creek Lookout Station but does not say it is this cabin; the story hedges that link. No access or current staffing information was found.
